# Introduction

The Transformer architecture replaced recurrence with attention and, in doing so,
unlocked a decade of scaling [@vaswani2017]. Yet most scaling studies treat the
attention mechanism as a black box, reporting only aggregate loss.

In this paper we ask a narrower question:

> Does the *shape* of the attention distribution carry signal about how well a
> model will generalize — and can we read that signal early?

We make three contributions:

- A measurement protocol for attention entropy that is stable across seeds.
- Evidence that entropy correlates with transfer accuracy across **six** model
  families.
- A practical early-stopping heuristic derived from the above.
